newsitem.title: UK: Actinor will retain listing - shareholder.
newsitem.headline: Actinor will retain listing - shareholder.

text.p: The new controlling shareholder in Norwegian ship investment firm Actinor Shipping ASA said on Wednesday it intends to maintain Actinor's Oslo listing while it considers future strategy.
Oyvind Gjerde, managing director of Paal Wilson & Co AS, told Reuters: "We will keep Actinor as a listed company while we look at various options."
"It is not decided yet what we are going to do with the company. There are several possible options."
Paal Wilson & Co and Hafslund Invest AS now control 97.6 percent of Actinor's shares after making a joint bid for the company earlier this summer, Actinor said.
Paal Wilson & Co, a privately-owned Norwegian shipping firm, alone controls over 60 percent of Actinor's equity.
"To be honest with you it is a slightly strange situation, since there is such a small float of shares now after the offer," Gjerde said.
"But we don't think we should delist the company while we are considering how to move forward."
Gjerde did not rule out an issue of new Actinor shares, but said he felt it "unlikely" in the near term.
"Actinor is in a good financial position at present, and has the finances for further expansion. There is no need for new money."
A decision will be taken on the future of the company "in the next year", said Gjerde.
He hinted that Actinor may become involved in ship operations, departing from its present strategy of making only financial investments in ships and offshore rigs.
Actinor was formed as a ship investment subsidiary of Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Hafslund Nycomed in the late 1980s, but demerged and listed in Oslo in May 1992.
It currently only invests in container, reefer and cruise ships and rigs which have long-term charter cover.
Actinor earlier reported first half pre-tax profits of 71 million Norwegian crowns, but warned second half results would be lower. --Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087/4012. Fax 5017
